title: Retired Educator Veronica Orduño Elected Laredo ISD Board President
excerpt: The Laredo Independent School District board of trustees elected retired educator Veronica Orduño as its new president in a unanimous vote Monday night.
content:
The Laredo Independent School District board of trustees elected retired educator Veronica Orduño as its new president in a unanimous vote at a meeting Monday night, according to KGNS.

Orduño has 36 years of experience in education, all of it in Laredo, and was first elected to the LISD board in November 2022. She represents District 7 and had served as board vice president for the past two years. She was elected president at the board’s 2026 reorganization meeting.

Orduño said the unanimous vote and the board’s confidence “means a lot to me.” She said her experience as a teacher and principal helps her keep students at the center of decisions.

Her stated focus is being an advocate for students, families and employees, and helping the district improve its state grade and student performance. The board also elected Hector “Tito” Garcia as vice president and Alma R. “Tita” Valdez as secretary.

The board’s district trustees are Jose “Chuy” Valdez Jr. (District 1), Juan “Johnny” Ramirez Jr. (District 2), Felix “Paco” Velasquez (District 3), Francisco “Frank” Tellez (District 4), Hector “Tito” Garcia (District 5), David “Dave” Gonzalez (District 6) and Veronica Orduño (District 7).

Source: KGNS, Nov. 17, 2026.
